payload.title: Rate-limit incoming webhooks per tenant
payload.goal: POST /webhooks answers 429 with a Retry-After header when one tenant sends more webhooks than the configured limit in the configured window. Put the limiter in src/lib/limiter.ts, wire it into src/routes/webhooks.ts (and src/app.ts if it needs shared state), and read the limit and the window through loadConfig() in src/config.ts with defaults. Add tests in test/webhooks.test.ts or a new test file.
acceptance: A tenant over the limit gets 429 with a Retry-After header
The limit and the window come from config, not constants in a route
The suite stays green with new tests for the 429 path

payload.text:
Done.

What I did:
- Kept `src/lib/limiter.ts` fixed-window per-key `RateLimiter` from the previous run.
- Kept `rateLimitMax` / `rateLimitWindowMs` in `src/config.ts` via `loadConfig()` (defaults 100 / 60000).
- Wired shared limiter state into `src/app.ts` (`Deps.limiter`, created in `createDeps`).
- `POST /webhooks` in `src/routes/webhooks.ts` checks the limiter per tenant after tenant validation and returns 429 JSON `{ error }` with a `Retry-After` header (seconds, rounded up) when over the limit; rejected requests are not stored or audited.
- Added `test/rate-limit.test.ts` with 429/Retry-After, per-tenant isolation, config-driven limit, no-store-on-429, and unit tests for window reset and Retry-After rounding.
- Updated `test/config.test.ts` expectations for the new config keys.
- Verified with `bun run test` (34 passed) and `bun run typecheck` (clean).

decision: per-tenant rate limiting uses an in-memory fixed-window counter keyed by tenant id with shared limiter state in Deps
decision: rate limit defaults are 100 requests per 60000ms via RATE_LIMIT_MAX and RATE_LIMIT_WINDOW_MS
decision: tests: test/config.test.ts changed because loadConfig gained rateLimitMax and rateLimitWindowMs so exact-match assertions needed the new keys

What I did not finish: nothing - all acceptance criteria are implemented.
What I did not look at: the review-voice-policy skill (not relevant to this task), and no other route groups beyond confirming Deps usage.
